subject: Private GPU pool: capacity forecast, traffic profile, and failover play
messages:
From: Sam Walters <sam.walters@sylvan-analytics.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@sylvan-analytics.com
Date: Mon, 13 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private deployment sizing request — Sylvan analytics forecast

Hi Irene / Laura,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We're moving from PoC to an expected private deployment and need a realistic capacity forecast + network checklist from Redwood for our procurement docs. High level ask: produce a sizing recommendation (GPU counts, headroom targets, autoscale bands), an estimated monthly committed throughput, and an ops playbook for on-call/network failover.

Key constraints and rough traffic profile (attached "sylvan_traffic_profile.csv"):
- Typical request: conversational generation with median sequence length ~ 48 tokens, 95th ~ 320 tokens, occasional long eval jobs up to 2,000 tokens.
- Expected baseline: 1,800 concurrent sessions during business hours (US PST), average request rate per session ~ 0.4 requests/minute.
- SLA: P95 latency for 512-token requests <= 350ms; P99 <= 900ms.
- Cache behavior: we expect ~55% prefix cache reuse for interactive flows.
- Network: single VPC with redundant top-of-rack (2 NICs), 100 Gbps uplinks, and private peering to our data center.
- Security: SOC2 controls required; vendor will do a short on-site network validation.

Procurement needs a 3-year commitment estimate; we'd like a staging runway (30% capacity) before full cutover. Can you run the numbers and propose a recommended cluster topology and failover options (regional fallback to hosted API or on-prem warm pool)?

Thanks — we need this by Wednesday (2026-12-16) to hit Sylvan's procurement review.

Cheers,
Sam
Sam Walters
Director, Platform Engineering | Sylvan Analytics

Attachments: sylvan_traffic_profile.csv, onprem_network_sketch_v2.pdf

Subject: Re: Private deployment sizing request — Sylvan analytics forecast

Hi Sam — thanks for the signal and the CSV. We're on it. Quick confirmation Qs before we size:
- Is the 1,800 concurrent sessions expected to sustain for the 8-hour business window or is that a peak lasting <30 minutes?
- Are long eval jobs (2k tokens) scheduled/batched (non-interactive) or could they occur during peak interaction hours?
- Do you expect encrypted NVMe for model artifacts locally, or will you use network-attached object storage with a local cache?

I'll loop Karthik for the GPU math and Marcus for network egress and procurement guidance. We'll produce:
1) a conservative capacity plan (sustained + 2x peak safety for P99),
2) an aggressive efficiency plan (quantization/packing and higher KV cache assumptions),
3) recommended autoscale bands and warm-pool sizing for a graceful cutover.

Deliverable ETA: initial draft tomorrow EOD (2026-12-14) and final by Wednesday.

Best,
Irene

Head of Solutions Architecture | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Walters <sam.walters@sylvan-analytics.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2026 11:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment sizing request — Sylvan analytics forecast

Folks — I ran a quick capacity sketch with the CSV assumptions and a conservative performance model for the Redwood serving runtime. Summary first, then reasoning and a short checklist.

Summary recommendation (initial):
- Target sustained throughput (interactive + background evals): ~20,000 tokens/s.
- Peak instantaneous throughput (95th-minute during business hours): ~60,000 tokens/s.
- Target GPU type: NVIDIA H100 80GB (fp16 mixed-precision), with an expected median generation latency per 512-token request ~ 180–250ms depending on batching.
- Effective tokens/sec per H100 (conservative): 3,000 tokens/s (assumes average batching and 55% prefix reuse).
- Raw GPU count (conservative): 20 H100s to hit sustained 20k tokens/s (20 * 3k = 60k tokens/s headroom). For P99 safety and autoscale cushion, plan committed baseline of 8 H100s (sustained baseline ~24k tokens/s) with an autoscale pool up to 28 H100s for peaks and long-eval absorption.

Sizing rationale & notes:
- Calculation: tokens/s per GPU = baseline_infer_throughput * batching_factor * cache_hit_multiplier. For our profile, "baseline_infer_throughput" per H100 (512-token frame) ~ 3k tps when using continuous batching and 55% KV reuse.
- Headroom: we recommend committed baseline to cover sustained load + 20% operational buffer. Autoscale band should add at least 2.5x of baseline for 99th-percentile peaks because long inferences (2k tokens) and evaluation jobs are bursty.
- Warm-pool strategy: keep a warm pool of 30% of autoscale max (e.g., if max 28, keep 8–9 GPUs warm) to keep cold-start latency below 250ms for first request. Warm pool is crucial for short, interactive SLAs.
- Network: plan for 100 Gbps per rack. For 28 H100s distributed across two racks, ensure cross-rack trunking with BGP failover and redundant 100 G uplinks. Egress to customer backbone should be provisioned at 150 G to handle bursts and model artifact transfers.
- Storage: local NVMe for model weights is strongly preferred for P95/P99 latency. If using remote object store, ensure prefetch + pro-active caching during warmup windows.
- Cost/commitment note: committing to 8 H100-equivalent baseline + scaling to 28 H100s when needed gives a reasonable compromise between cost and latency guarantees. We'll provide monthly projected token burn in the final sheet.

Operational playbook (short):
- Pre-cutover: run a 72-hour soak against staging with traffic shaped to 1.25x expected baseline and verify P99 tail.
- Network failover: configure a regional fallback route to Redwood Hosted API (tiered) with automatic rate-limited spillover. Fallback policy: spill 40% of non-sensitive traffic to hosted API when local CPU queue depth exceeds threshold for >30s.
- Monitoring signals: token processing backlog, KV cache hit-rate, per-GPU utilization, NIC saturation, median P95/P99 latency. Alert thresholds: GPU util > 85% sustained (5m), cache-hit < 40%, NIC utilization > 80% (1m).

Open items for Sam:
- Confirm whether long eval jobs can be scheduled to off-peak windows (evening) or must be mixed with interactive traffic. Scheduling those will materially reduce peak GPU requirements.
- Confirm storage choice (local NVMe vs network object store).

I attached a quick "initial_sizing_table.xlsx" with two scenarios (conservative / efficiency) and per-month committed tokens estimate.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Systems Engineer | Redwood Inference

Sam — quick ops + procurement note from my side.

Network and procurement next steps:
- We'll schedule an on-site network test during the staging window (2027-01-10 to 2027-01-14). Please confirm rack availability and remote console access.
- Procurement: if you commit to baseline 8 H100s for 12 months we can provide a blended committed pricing that includes 30% warm-pool credit. I'll work with finance to put a proposal together; expects a draft by Friday.
- Change control: we'll require a cutover runbook sign-off with a rollback plan to the staged warm pool + hosted spillover. I'll attach the draft runbook to the Jira ticket RWI-1428.

I'll coordinate with infra to reserve two 100 G uplinks per rack and set up BGP sessions for redundancy. Irene/Karthik — can you confirm the warm-pool size you want reserved in our Draft PO? Karthik suggested 8–9 GPUs; we should lock a number for procurement.

Marcus Lin
Senior Product Manager, Dedicated & Private | Redwood Inference
